overview: White challenges d5 from the flank without committing a central pawn, then usually fianchettoes with g3 and Bg2 and castles. Black can take on c4, hold d5 with ...c6 or ...e6 (a Slav or QGD-like set-up), or push ...d4. The game stays flexible, with transpositions to the English, Catalan or Queen's Gambit.

white_ideas.idea: Fianchetto the king's bishop (g3, Bg2) and pressure d5 and the long diagonal
Keep d-pawn flexible, choose between d4 and a slower e4 break later
Regain c4 pawn if Black takes, with Qa4+ or Ne5 and queenside pressure

black_ideas.idea: Hold the d5 centre with ...c6 or ...e6 and develop naturally
Take on c4 and aim to hold or give back the pawn for free development

typical_structures.structure: Slav or QGD-like structures with White's bishop on g2 instead of d3
Reversed Benoni or English structures after ...d4

character.notes: Positional manoeuvring, small edges, little forced theory. Neither sharp nor especially hard to crack.

gambit.notes: 2...dxc4 can be won back by force or without risk, so not a gambit.

structure.notes: Centre not yet determined, flank opening with tension on d5 and c4.

approach.notes: Typical flexible set-up (Nf3, c4, g3, Bg2, O-O) playable against most defences, a hypermodern system.

level.notes: Clear flexible plans, little to memorise, accessible to club players.

sublines_that_differ.name: Réti: 2...d4 Benoni-style
sublines_that_differ.how: Black grabs space, gives a reversed Benoni with a more open game.

character.reason: Flexible and positional without being especially hard to break or tactical.

gambit.reason: No material is given that cannot be regained.

soundness.reason: Played regularly at the top level.

structure.reason: Flank opening with the centre left undecided.

approach.reason: Nf3, c4, g3, Bg2 set-up playable against most defences.

level.reason: Flexible plans but subtle move orders against varied defences.

plans.reason: Long diagonal bishop and flank pressure on d5.
